topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the course by introducing the scope of cancer biology, the teaching structure, and the lecture's core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and tissue architectural foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental concept of cancer as a multi-step disruption of normal genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Pathology and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors transition from localized, benign lesions into invasive and metastatic malignancies using histological and anatomical evidence.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and pathophysiological causes of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the clinical classification systems for tumors and the physiological mechanisms through which benign and malignant growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the epidemiological frequency of major cancer types in humans alongside the comparative incidence of neoplasms across companion animals and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and organ-specific modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, histological basis, and diagnostic methods used to detect early pre-invasive and malignant lesions in clinical screening programs.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practicals and lectures.
